name: background.add
doc: GNOME's Add Picture, {path} → {path, copied}: the picture copied into ~/.local/share/backgrounds as <YYYY-mm-dd-HH-MM-SS>-<name> (a picture already there is not copied again); event background.changed {what: added, path}.

name: background.catalog
doc: GNOME Settings' background chooser, {} → {items: [{name (WinPoint's language), path, dark (the filename-dark twin or null), options (picture-options), slideshow, preview (a slideshow's first picture), source}], own: [{path, name, modified}] (the user's pictures in ~/.local/share/backgrounds, newest first), folder}: gnome-background-properties/*.xml of the system data dirs, then the user's.

name: background.remove
doc: Remove one of the user's pictures, {path} (a file directly in ~/.local/share/backgrounds, never through a symlink): moved to the trash as GNOME Settings does; event background.changed {what: removed, path}.

name: notifications.app.set
doc: One app's GNOME notification settings, {appId: desktop id, values: {key: bool}} (the six keys of notifications.apps) → {appId, canonical, path, listed, items}: the relocatable org.gnome.desktop.notifications.application with its application-id, then the app in application-children, as GNOME Shell records an app (amendment 6); event notifications.changed {what: app, appId, canonical}.

name: notifications.apps
doc: GNOME Settings' App Notifications, {} → {apps: [{id, canonical, path, name, icon, usesNotifications, listed, values: {enable, enable-sound-alerts, show-banners, force-expanded, show-in-lock-screen, details-in-lock-screen}, locked: [key]}]}: the apps with X-GNOME-UsesNotifications and those in org.gnome.desktop.notifications application-children, by name.

name: privacy.app
doc: One app as GNOME Settings' Apps page shows it, {id: desktop id, sizes?: false skips the disk walk}: kind (flatpak, snap, host), portalId, version, storage {app, data, cache, total}, canClearCache, permissions (PermissionStore rows: key, table, id, set, allowed), background {set, allowed}, autostart {enabled}, searchProvider {desktopId, defaultDisabled}, globalShortcuts {appId, shortcuts: [{id, description, accels}]}, required (flatpak static permissions or snap plugs with their slots) and handlers (file and link types: type, kind, name, extensions, isDefault).

name: privacy.app.clearCache
doc: Empty a Flatpak app's ~/.var/app/<id>/cache, {id} (GNOME's Clear Cache); answers {freed} in bytes.

name: privacy.app.globalShortcuts.set
doc: Rebind an app's global shortcuts through xdg-desktop-portal-gnome's org.gnome.GlobalShortcutsRebind, {id, shortcuts?: [{id, accels: [GTK accelerator]}], clear?: true removes every binding}.

name: privacy.app.removeHandler
doc: Stop an app from opening one file or link type, {id, type} (g_app_info_remove_supports_type: [Removed Associations] of mimeapps.list).

name: privacy.app.resetHandlers
doc: Reset the associations of every type an app opens, {id}, or of every type the user's mimeapps.list names, {all: true} (g_app_info_reset_type_associations); answers {types}.

name: privacy.app.setAutostart
doc: Start an app at log-in or not, {id, on}: the user's ~/.config/autostart/<id> with X-GNOME-Autostart-enabled, a copy of the app's desktop file when it has none (as GNOME Settings).

name: privacy.app.snapConnect
doc: Connect or disconnect a snap's plug, {id, plug, slot?: {snap, slot}, connect}, through snapd (POST /v2/interfaces with X-Allow-Interaction: snapd asks for the password through polkit).

name: privacy.apps.sandboxed
doc: The installed sandboxed apps, {} → {apps: [{id (desktop id), portalId (the PermissionStore's app id: a Flatpak id or snap.<name>), kind (flatpak|snap), name (WinPoint's language), icon}]}, by name: the permission pages (Locatie, Camera, Microfoon) name the store's apps with it.

name: privacy.deletePermission
doc: Remove an app's value from a PermissionStore entry, {table, id, app}, or the whole entry without app; only the entries GNOME Settings shows.

name: privacy.insights.get
doc: Ubuntu's system reports (amendment 38), {} → {available, sources: {linux, ubuntu_release_upgrader}: true|false|null (null: no consent file yet, shown off)}: ubuntu-insights consent <source> through tools::system_tool.

name: privacy.insights.report
doc: "Diagnostische gegevens weergeven" (GNOME's Show Report), {source?: linux} → {source, report (the JSON report, indented)}: ubuntu-insights collect --dry-run, which writes and sends nothing; one at a time (busy privacy.reportBusy); {cancel: true} stops a running one (GNOME's Cancel Report Generation), which then answers cancelled privacy.reportCancelled.

name: privacy.insights.set
doc: {source: linux|ubuntu_release_upgrader, consent: bool} → {source, consent}: ubuntu-insights consent <source> --state true|false (the user's ~/.config/ubuntu-insights/<source>-consent.toml); event privacy.changed {what: insights, source}.

name: privacy.permissions
doc: A PermissionStore entry, {table, id} (location/location, devices/camera, devices/microphone, screenshot, wallpaper, background, gnome/shortcuts-inhibitor): {available, apps: [{app, value, allowed}]}.

name: privacy.reports.get
doc: Ubuntu's error reports (GNOME Settings' Ubuntu Diagnostics), {} → {available, mode: never|auto|manual, reportCrashes, automatic}: whoopsie-preferences' ReportCrashes and AutomaticallyReportCrashes on the system bus; available false without the daemon.

name: privacy.reports.set
doc: "Foutrapporten naar Canonical verzenden", {mode: never|auto|manual} → {mode, reportCrashes, automatic}: whoopsie-preferences SetReportCrashes then SetAutomaticallyReportCrashes with interactive authorization (polkit com.ubuntu.whoopsiepreferences.change); event privacy.changed {what: reports, mode}.

name: privacy.searchProviders
doc: GNOME's search providers (Zoekmachtigingen), {} → {providers: [{desktopId, name (WinPoint's language), icon, defaultDisabled}]}: gnome-shell/search-providers/*.ini of the system data dirs whose DesktopId is an installed app, by name; whether each shows results and their order are org.gnome.desktop.search-providers disabled/enabled/sort-order, which Settings binds.

name: privacy.security
doc: GNOME Settings' Device Security, read only, {} → {available, hsi (fwupd's HostSecurityId), level (0-5 or null), runtimeIssue, secureBoot: on|off|problem|null, attrs and events: [{appstreamId, title, level, result, previous, flags, success, runtimeIssue, obsoleted, created, plugin}], daemonVersion, vendor, product, securityCenter (Ubuntu's Security Center is installed)}: fwupd's properties, GetHostSecurityAttrs and GetHostSecurityEvents(10) on the system bus.

name: privacy.securityCenter.open
doc: Start Ubuntu's Security Center (the desktop-security-center snap), {} → {id, via: shell|host}: through launchBridge.js launch.app as GNOME Shell's child, else through apps.launch as GNOME Settings starts it; not_found privacy.securityCenterMissing when it is not installed; a dry run starts nothing.

name: privacy.setPermission
doc: Set an app's value in a PermissionStore entry, {table, id, app, value: true/false (GNOME's own values) or the strings}; event privacy.changed.
